message.content:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, symmetric hilar lymph node enlargement with well-defined margins and clear lung fields (no parenchymal opacities), which is the classic radiographic presentation of Stage I sarcoidosis. This symmetry and lack of infiltrates help distinguish it from malignancy (often asymmetric/irregular), tuberculosis (often unilateral/calcified), or infectious processes (which typically show pulmonary opacities).
